title: dev.qory.run.started
description: The run is open: Forager's open of the run at its gateway wrote it, before the run's host work, such as a fetch, and before any session joins the run. The first event of a run in the file, after dev.qory.run.registered where there is one, and the event a receiver creates the run on. What each session starts is in its dev.qory.session.started. Each of host, wall, a label's key and value, and about's kind, title and subjects' titles that contains qak_ or qrk_ in any case is `(a name that contains an access key secret)` in its place, or `(a name that contains a run key)` when it contains qrk_ and no qak_. Each string of about's details that contains one is `(a value that contains an access key secret)` or `(a value that contains a run key)` in the same way, and a member name of details is the name's phrase. A subject whose type or ref contains one is left out, and so is a subject's url that contains one.

opened_by.description: What opened the run: run, Forager's open of a run at its gateway, which writes this event once, before any session joins the run.

forager_version.description: The version of the Forager that opened the run.

host.description: The host name of the machine the run was opened on, the one its sessions run on.

wall.description: The adapter that builds the enclosure each session of the run runs in: docker. Absent when the run has no wall.

machine.description: The adapter that made the machine the run was opened on, such as aws-ec2, or none when no adapter made it. It is 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -, the first a letter. Absent when the caller passes none.

setup.description: Where the run's setup commands run, or would run if it had any: outside, in a container apart from the agent's, or inside, in the agent's container before the runtime starts. Absent when the run has nowhere to run setup commands.

labels.description: The caller's names for the run, its key in a queue, a repository, an issue, as the command that started the run received them. Forager copies them and reads nothing into them, except that a separate gateway's selection of credentials can take a credential's argument from one. Only this event contains them among the events, and the gateway's registration of the run sends them in its body, never in a URL; a receiver keeps them with the run it creates on it. Of two labels whose keys become the same phrase, the one whose key sorts first is sent.

enum: (a name that contains an access key secret)
(a name that contains a run key)

about.description: What the run is about, as the caller passed it: the kind of run, a title, the subjects it works on and details, every member optional. Forager copies it and reads nothing into it. Only this event contains it among the events, and the gateway's registration of the run sends it in its body; it never selects or changes a security policy. An empty about is left out; an about whose every member is left out for a secret is sent as {}. No string in it, key or value, contains a control character: U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F, U+2028 and U+2029. Forager alone checks these rules, which the schema cannot state: the byte limits, the 8192 bytes of details, that no two subjects have the same type and ref, a url's syntax and host, that a url carries no user name or password, and that no member name appears twice in details. Of two members of details whose names become the same phrase, the first is sent; details that grow past 8192 bytes by their phrases are left out. Each maxLength counts characters and is an upper bound of the byte limit the description states.

kind.description: The kind of run, the caller's word, at most 64 bytes.

title.description: The run's title, at most 256 bytes.

subjects.description: What the run works on, 1 to 16. No two subjects have the same type and ref: a subject is identified by its type and ref.

type.description: The subject's type, an open name the caller chooses: words of a-z and 0-9, each joined to the next by one space, underscore, dot or dash, at most 64 bytes.

ref.description: The subject's reference, at most 256 bytes.

url.description: Where the subject is shown: an absolute http or https URL, at most 2048 bytes. A url never carries a user name or password.

title.description: The subject's title, at most 256 bytes.

details.description: A JSON object of the caller's, at most 8192 bytes as this event contains it, compacted, with <, > and & written as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026, and nested at most 4 levels deep: details is level 1, and an object or an array inside it is level 2. A key is 1 to 64 bytes. It is shown to every reader of the run, so it never holds a secret.

about_details_1.description: Level 1: details itself, an object of scalars and level 2 objects and arrays.

about_details_2.description: Level 2: an object or an array of scalars and level 3 objects and arrays.

about_details_3.description: Level 3: an object or an array of scalars and level 4 objects and arrays.

about_details_4.description: Level 4, the deepest: an object or an array of scalars only.
